== Original post ==

'''Lingrell's Hyperbounce'''
* '''Author:''' Scott "CRingwell" Lingrell
* '''Published:''' September 7, 2005
* '''Rating:''' 4.78
* '''Description:''' A True Rogue deck. Not for beginners or anyone else for that matter.

=== Strategy ===

This is a very tricky deck to play.  Its probably the my favorite deck since Thone Room Odds that Lolli and I made from RamapoCon 99.

This is the deck that has won me the NY states and also went undefeated in NYC's event earlier in the year.  Plus about 30 other games online and such, losing about 3-5 of them. (against certain scum decks and Fear D* decks).

This deck is a pain in the wookie to play against.

This deck started from my not broken Heroic Sacrifice deck I beat Drew Scott with at Mystic Visions (by luck) and knew the basic idea was a good one.

After that, with Krayt Dragon Howl (V) letting me start Obi-Wan (regardless of objective restrictions) and his saber was excellent for card economy and a quick first turn force loss of 3.

That was offset by no starting effects and only a 3 card hand (but I could activate 3 from the starting interrupt going back to my hand via the text) which allowed me to maximize the use of It Can Wait.

With the activation early, the ability to play droids/Mace quickly to help reinforce the site for turn 2 and beyond, I knew a nice steady drain of 3/4/5 would help me quickly cause a force loss they did not want to lose.

The deck never plays the same way twice.  But the main goal is to flip, then do hit an runs with The Dynamic Duo (Pancake and Queen) wherever possible, playing the Destiny Adder for them for 3 destiny (which then allows you to take the destiny adder back into hand) and coupled with Dont Forget The Droids (V) stops them from getting destiny, allowing them to keep running around and retrieving while Lando, Qui-Gon and Tawss (V) do what they can to offset the opponent.

The biggest strengths of this deck are card economy, and the card advantage I get from always having a ton of force mid-late game to keep me alive and allow me to keep picking at them with credits (stacking 8-10 cards is normal).

Some of the problems with the deck are decks that run heavy Sac and are able to deploy a Maul/Vader turn 1 with Sense to cancel the ICW, Colo for the deestiny to make sure I don't have a chance to stick around for the next turn.  That can hurt but with today's meta being 2-3 Dark Senses, I have just as much chance of canceling thier Sense (3 Sense combo, 2 Alter, 2 Control combo) that I normally can get what I need (if they come after me).

Most decks don't have the ability to come down turn one but if they do, it just gets bounced.  The interrupt choices are a bit different from other versions but the choices are clear.

They really don't know what to grab. (here is a hint - do not grab It Can Wait).  Because if they do, you can then play It Could Be Worse and Were Doomed without reservation.

Why not?...

Retrieval - I took out Edge and Noble Sacrifice because I found myself never playing it with Secret Plans and also realizing I could retrieve 5-10 cards with battles anyway and one Edge could counteract that with Code Clearance Shield.

Rebels - I actually had Chewbacca in the deck originally (and thought about Jedi Luke) in case of non-Jabba's Prize CCT.  But its so far from ever happening.  Either way, Jedi Luke isnt a bad idea (you can free him and use him well!).

Scum Hate - The deck has an obvious issue with scum decks (even though I did well against NY States barely winning by 1 card in the final confrontation) Mandalorian Mishap is a good card to add 3/4 of.  You can easily cut some fluff and add some in if you want.

2 Queens - I swapped out a Padme for the secondary use of A Remote Planet, helping vs Tatooine based decks, making all thier drains -1 there.

Cards I would like to add in:

Its A Hit! x2

Nabrun (took it out for this version but its card 61)

Have fun.  Its definately a fun deck that gives you plenty of options.
